messages:
Sam: CI alerted on the nightly quant-eval: BERTScore collapsed to 0.0 for all samples. quick glance shows zeros in the scorer logs. anyone seen this pattern before?
Anya: saw few flakes yesterday, but didn't dig in. can you paste the scorer logs?
Sam: log excerpt:
```
INFO compute_bertscore: raw_scores = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
WARNING aggregator mean -> 0.0
```
Sam: pass@k on same seed also dipped from 0.42 -> 0.33 which is weird. suspect two separate causes.
Mike: two axes: (1) scoring pipeline converting dtypes wrong, (2) runner sampling/order nondeterminism. which repos touched scoring?
Sam: scoring lives in inference/eval/metrics/bertscore.py. dug into the quantized run outputs: embeddings produced as float16. scorer does something like `np.round(scores, 3).astype(np.int32)` before binning/aggregation. that truncates everything <1 to 0.
Anya: wait we cast floats to int for calibration bins? that's a bug. calibration needs floats.
Sam: exact snippet I found: 
```
# problematic
scores = np.round(scores, 3).astype(np.int32)
bin_idx = scores // 1
```
Sam: result: every score <1 becomes 0 -> all bins collapse -> mean -> 0.0
Mike: yikes. fix: keep scores as float, do aggregation in float64. no int casts. also don't round before aggregation.
Jordan: on pass@k nondet: runner collects candidate set via set() and then samples; Python set iteration order changed across versions. that makes selection order vary and pass@k fluctuate.
Anya: pass@k requires reproducible candidate ordering or explicit RNG seeding. prefer preserving insertion order or sorting the candidates.
Sam: proposed code changes in my head:
- scorer: `scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64); agg = float(np.mean(scores))`
- calibration: use quantile bins (equal-count) not integer bins; use sklearn.calibration_curve(..., strategy='quantile')
- runner: replace set() with `list(sorted(candidates))` or preserve insertion order from generator
Mike: add unit tests: `tests/eval/test_bertscore_dtype_handling.py` that feeds float16-like numbers and asserts avg > 0.01; and `tests/eval/test_passatk_determinism.py` that seeds RNG and checks identical selections across runs.
Sam: also add a tiny fixture `tests/fixtures/quant_small.jsonl` used by CI small-quant-eval job so we run the quantized eval path on PRs.
Jordan: CI gating: please add a reporter that fails the run when any critical-suite metric regresses >8% vs baseline. post to #eng-ml on failure. avoid silent degradations.
Anya: for calibration visuals, equal-count bins avoid empty bins caused by int truncation. `calibration_curve(y_true, y_prob, n_bins=10, strategy='quantile')` is straightforward and stable.
Sam: repro snippet to include in PR description:
```
scores = np.array([0.012, 0.045, 0.003], dtype=np.float16)
# bad path
s = np.round(scores, 3).astype(np.int32)
print(s)  # -> [0 0 0]
# good path
print(np.mean(scores.astype(np.float64)))  # -> ~0.0193
```
Mike: perfect repro. also add a linter/test to catch `.astype(np.int32)` in metrics modules. or at least a codeowner review.
Sam: opening PR now with fixes + tests + small CI job + changelog entry + README note about dtype expectations and deterministic ordering. will tag reviewers.
Sam: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pull/1327 (includes tests and CI job yaml `ci/jobs/small-quant-eval.yml`)
Anya: quick review queued. once green let's merge and watch nightly runs.
eval-bot: queued small-quant-eval for PR #1327 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Jordan: after merge i'll re-run the full nightly benchmark and the regression detector.
Sam: follow-up action: update `eval-runner/README.md` to mention deterministic candidate ordering, required input dtypes (float32/64), and recommended calibration strategy.
Mike: thanks, this should unflake a bunch of quant-related eval noise.
Sam: will monitor post-merge and post the nightly diff in #eng-ml.
